items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: Henry Allen, I think Paul Barberin was in for a while, and he was always trying to get a new band together. Somehow I never got to that rehearsal

ctx.x: I have a note here. He mentioned that there were

three great clarinetists in New Orleans. Piku, Lorenzo Tio, and George Bakke. He didn't think Big Eye Louie was really in the first class. Other people will tell you they think Big Eye was better than Piku and so on. So some of that could be a question of opinion. he thought Dodds wasn't really a first class clarinetist. He was all right. He was only on a couple of his records, maybe four sides or so. I don't know. I even asked him once, I said, is it true that Muggsy had recorded with him? And he said, yes. No,…
He was dead in that two summer.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I gave you a thing where I interviewed Paul Barberin about Wilton Crawley's teeth falling out.

ctx.x: Well, I remember all the little white pieces of paper, you know, the official two-lane things.

Oh, no, no, no. I gave you a thing where I interviewed Paul Barberin about Wilton Crawley's teeth falling out. It was a supplement. This doesn't go on the tape. It was really funny. It was a funny story that Paul Barberin told me.
The funniest story on Wilton Crawley is the one that Bob Green interviewed Manzi Campbell. How do you spell Manzi Campbell? With a Z or an S?
